newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close down, led by blue chips.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close down, led by blue chips.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed lower on Wednesday, led by declines in high capitalised blue chips and a round of profit-taking, brokers said.
The all share index closed 4.19 points down at 607.69. Among blue chips, Development Finance Corp fell five rupees to 285, and John Keells Holdings dropped 1.25 to 191.75.
But brokers said the index seemed set for a recovery.
"The index could turn when retail investors return soon...," said Hussain Gani a trader at brokerage John Keells.
Retail investors have reaped over 10 percent among liquid shares in the past two months following a rise in the index to 630 points from 550, he said.
A few local institutional investors were also active, although many who were over exposed remained sidelined.

"We started buying slowly after the index showed very firm resistance at 550 points," said Gihan Rajapakse, fund manager, CTC Eagle Fund Management. The company is focusing on "forgotten stocks which will show growth", he said.
Turnover rose to 104.4 million rupees on 1.1 million shares. Foreign buying was 65 million rupees and selling, 47.8 million.
